properties.statement: The permit digest uses EIP-712 name, version, chainId and permit-authority verifying contract and binds all 26 permit fields, the 17-field release and three-field kernel envelope.
A successful consume requires the current signer epoch and exact per-repository nonce, permanently consumes the repository lineage and launchId, and advances the nonce only on success.
Permit cancellation, approval-generation cancellation, signer disabling, time bounds and release retirement/deactivation fail closed without consuming a reusable nonce before one successful launch.
Release generations are monotonic and bind exact authority, verifier, registry, profile, route, runtime code hashes, route writer authority and execution authority.
CREATE2 predictions bind wrapper deployer, salts, initcode, token and derived NFT metadata, renderer, ticks, price and recipients; direct implementation deployment cannot occupy the wrapper graph.

The wrapper accepts only launch from its immutable route, verifies the implementation runtime hash again before delegatecall, rejects fallback selectors and preserves the reviewed slot-zero mapping layout.
Permit consumption and the full atomic launch entrypoint are guarded by Cancun transient-storage reentrancy locks; external effects revert atomically on callback failure.
The canonical hook declares both beforeSwapReturnDelta and afterSwapReturnDelta and uses signed hook deltas to retain only the ETH fee while preserving PoolManager delta settlement.
When ETH is specified and a beforeSwap fee cannot be corrected on the unspecified return-delta side, any partial fill is rejected and leaves no fee; complete fills at the limit remain valid.

The hook permits only native ETH versus its immutable SHARD token, exact pool fee, tick spacing, hook address and reviewed start price, and rejects swaps before one-shot initialization or through a foreign pool.
Every swap quadrant charges the inclusive ETH fee with carried remainders; builder plus Programmable plus holder accounting conserves every wei and fees remain covered by ETH or ERC-6909 claims.

Permit consumption, repository marking, factory deployment, graph validation and registry registration occur in one transaction so any downstream failure rolls every effect back and permits an exact retry.
Repository uniqueness lives permanently in the stable Permit Authority across signer epochs, release generations and competing real route stacks; registry retry idempotence does not weaken it.

Finalization requires the observed block, transaction identity, configured minimum depth, nonzero one-use evidence and canonical observed and confirmed-head block hashes inside the native blockhash window.
A reorg or stale proof fails closed when either supplied historical block hash differs from blockhash; unavailable history beyond 256 blocks cannot be treated as canonical evidence.
Observed becomes finalized or terminally revoked; revision one and fee claims remain immutable, approval, deployment and evidence are one-use, and revocation cannot be repaired by record rewrite.
Permit and registry authority classes are distinct at construction and permanently lineage-separated; the immutable route is the sole registry writer and wrapper launch caller.
